title: Shadow-swap dual-serve caused model divergence; recovery playbook and automation
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Summary: During a staged rollout we observed a ~12% subset of production traffic being accidentally served by both the stable model and a new experimental variant (dual-serve) due to a mis-application of the shadow-swap policy in the routing mesh. This caused request duplication, increased token costs, and observable output divergence for several customers. This ticket captures the post-incident analysis, immediate mitigations, and action items to prevent recurrence, including a recovery playbook and automation proposals.
impact_summary:
- Affected customers: 9 accounts with medium-to-high traffic; two experienced SLA violations due to latency spikes.
- Cost impact: estimated additional token spend of $24k over the 3-hour window.
- Quality: 0.8% of responses across sampled traffic showed semantic divergence triggering alerting rules.
- Availability: no full service outage; some routes had elevated 95th/99th latency leading to throttling behavior.
timeline: 2026-02-15 09:12 UTC - Rollout pipeline triggered for model v2.3-experimental (shadow-swap variant).
2026-02-15 09:18 UTC - Monitoring alert: unexpected duplicate upstream requests detected for route /chat.generate. Increased p50->p95 latency.
2026-02-15 09:22 UTC - Oncall paged; initial mitigation toggled shadow-swap to passive mode (manual).
2026-02-15 09:35 UTC - Confirmed 12% of traffic was matched by both stable and experimental backends due to routing affinity flag mismatch introduced in rollout config.
2026-02-15 10:05 UTC - Emergency rollback of rollout config; routing restored but some sessions remained pinned due to KV pinning TTLs.
2026-02-15 11:30 UTC - Post-rollback validation completed; traffic duplication ceased; follow-up ticket opened for automation and runbook improvements (this ticket).
root_cause: A recent change in the rollout controller (PR #7281) added a shadow-swap mode intended to mirror traffic to an experimental backend without altering client affinity. A tiny regression in matching precedence allowed the shadow and primary route predicates to both evaluate true for a subset of session cookies when routing affinity and cookie-ttl were present. The controller then emitted dual forwarding actions for those requests. The defect was a precedence inversion in the router predicate evaluation and insufficient integration tests for cookie-affinity edge cases.
steps_taken: Immediate: Disabled shadow-swap globally within 8 minutes of detection, then applied a targeted route predicate fix to prevent dual-forwarding.
Corrective: Reverted PR #7281 to restore previous stable predicate ordering; rolled out hotfix in runtime-1.28-hotfix.
detection: Detected by duplicate-request metric (duplicate_upstream_requests) which increased from baseline 0.01% to 12% and by customer latency SLO alerts. The observability dashboard correlation between duplicate requests and route predicates made diagnosis straightforward once routed logs were expanded.
postmortem_findings: Testing gap: unit and integration tests did not include cookie-affinity + shadow-swap combinations.
Runbook gap: no immediate, automated mitigation for dual-forwarding; manual disable was error-prone.
Tooling gap: rollout preview UI did not surface combined predicate evaluation for session-level keys.
action_items: (A1) Add regression tests that exercise cookie-affinity + shadow-swap predicate combinations. Owner: Priya Shah. Due: 2026-02-28.
(A2) Implement a guard that prevents a route from emitting >1 forward action per request in the routing mesh at the controller level (circuit breaker). Owner: Connor Li. Due: 2026-03-10.
(A3) Automate an emergency 'shadow-unwind' play that can be toggled via Console and API to forcibly quash mirror actions for a route. Owner: Marco Hernández. Due: 2026-03-05.
(A4) Enhance rollout preview UI to show evaluated predicates and final decision for sample sessions (include cookie TTL, affinity token). Owner: UX: Lina Park, Eng: Rui Zhang. Due: 2026-03-24.
(A5) Backfill e2e test harness to run staged rollouts against synthetic session traffic with pinned cookies and TTL churn. Owner: QA: Ben Curtis. Due: 2026-03-12.
(A6) Add a monitoring alert to trigger when duplicate_upstream_requests > 0.5% for >5min and bind an automated throttle action. Owner: SRE: Zoe Miller. Due: 2026-02-25.

(A7) Update runbook: include steps to detect dual-forwarding, safe rollback order, KV TTL invalidation checklist, and recommended post-rollback validation queries. Owner: Oncall lead: Aisha Raman. Due: 2026-02-20.
(A8) Post-deployment: perform a chaos test that simulates predicate inversion on staging to validate guardrails. Owner: Resilience team: Omar Ali. Due: 2026-04-01.
validation_plan: After implementing A1-A6, run a controlled shadow-swap deployment in staging with 100k synthetic sessions using pinned cookies and randomized TTL churn. Verify duplicate_upstream_requests remains at baseline, confirm guard prevents >1 forward action per request, and confirm UI shows evaluated predicates correctly. Document results in Confluence and link to dashboard.
follow_up_notes: We identified a separate minor issue where KV TTL invalidation lagged behind routing changes; additional instrumentation (A9) recommended if A1-A6 fixes do not fully prevent session-level anomalies.
Recommend cross-team retro with PM/Design/SRE to review rollout UX and error surface decisions (scheduled 2026-03-08).
